justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: No published RCTs or comparative studies of BCPR vs non-certified OT outcomes.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Portfolio plus exam process; significant documentation and time requirements.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to OT in physical rehabilitation settings; moderately broad within hospital and outpatient rehab.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: No BCPR billing impact; professional signaling credential only.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Limited employer recognition outside OT professional community; lower demand than ABPTS board certs.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: Credential recognition limited outside OT professional community.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: Physical rehab OT board cert addresses populations (stroke, ortho, neuro) typically funded by insurance/Medicare, not cash-pay consumers.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: No direct consumer brand recognition; doesn't justify premium cash rates in a private practice.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Rare among OTs (under 1% hold AOTA board certs) but consumers don't recognize it, so differentiation is professional, not commercial.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Tied to individual clinician credential; can support a niche program but staffing other BCPRs is hard given small pool.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Virtually unknown to direct consumers; demand exists only in institutional hiring.
justifications.business.efficiency: Requires portfolio submission, years of practice, and significant cost — slow path to a credential with low cash-pay ROI.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: AOTA board certification is the OT analog to ABPTS specialties and is explicitly valued for OT faculty promotion and tenure files.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Portfolio process requires scholarly reflection; holders often publish, though not at the volume of residency-trained PTs.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Directly maps to physical-disabilities curricular content in MOT/OTD programs.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Underlying interventions (neurorehab, ortho OT) have a solid but mixed evidence base.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Frequently listed as preferred in OT faculty postings, particularly for phys-dys course leads.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Multi-year portfolio process is moderately burdensome relative to academic payoff.
